title: Gunfire Outside Diljit Dosanjh Manager Home; Bishnoi Gang Claims Attack
excerpt: Shots fired at manager Gurpartap Singh Kang residence in Haryana as notorious gang escalates threats against Punjabi entertainment figures
body:
Unidentified gunmen opened fire outside the Karnal, Haryana residence of Gurpartap Singh Kang, the longtime manager of global Punjabi music icon Diljit Dosanjh, in a late-night attack that has jolted India celebrity security landscape. No injuries were reported, but the Lawrence Bishnoi gang swiftly claimed responsibility through social media posts attributed to associates identified as Tyson Bishnoi, Aarzoo Bishnoi, and Hari Boxer.

**The Threat Escalation:** The gang alleged that Austrian-made weapons were used in the attack, framing it as a warning rather than an extortion bid. In their posts, the group accused Dosanjh management team of misconduct involving women during his recent Australia concert tour — claims that remain unverified. Karnal police have launched an investigation and are working to authenticate the social media posts, though initial assessments reportedly treated the incident with skepticism, with some local officers initially calling it a rumor before evidence of discharged rounds emerged.

**A Pattern of Celebrity Targeting:** The Lawrence Bishnoi criminal network, operating largely from behind bars through jailed leader Lawrence Bishnoi and Canada-based associate Goldy Brar, has systematically targeted Punjabi entertainment and Bollywood figures for years. The gang is widely believed to be behind the 2022 assassination of rapper Sidhu Moosewala, and has issued threats against Salman Khan, comedian Munawar Faruqui, and multiple other public figures. Just days ago, Delhi Police foiled a separate plot linked to the Brar faction targeting Faruqui, arresting two suspects after a pre-dawn shootout in the capital.

**The Diaspora Dimension:** For the estimated 4.4 million Indian-Americans and millions more in Canada, the UK, and Australia who pack Diljit Dosanjh stadium tours, the attack strikes an unsettling chord. Dosanjh Dil-Luminati world tour has made him the most commercially successful Punjabi artist in Western markets, and his management team coordinates massive international logistics. The gang reach into diaspora communities — Brar operates from Canada, and Bishnoi network has demonstrated transnational capability — raises questions about whether Indian-origin entertainment professionals face security risks that extend well beyond Mumbai.

**What to Watch:** Karnal police verification of the gang claims will be critical. If confirmed, expect intensified security protocols across the Punjabi entertainment industry and renewed pressure on Indian and Canadian authorities to dismantle the Bishnoi network cross-border operations.
